items.title: 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party
items.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed a suit seeking to compel Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register a political association as Wisdom Party (WP), 88 days to the 2027 presidential election. Justice James Omotosho, in a judgment, held that the plaintiff’s claim lacked merit and the suit had become academic. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plaintiff, Chief Mrs Chinasa Nwekeke, had filed the suit as the pro tem National Chairman and on behalf of Wisdom Party, a political association seeking a registration as a party. Nwekeke, in the originating summons marked FHC//ABJ/CS/746/2026 filed on April 14 by her lawyer, Mark Agbo, had sued INEC as the sole defendant. The plaintiff sought a declaration that the political association, “Wisdom Party”, to which INEC did not object to its name, symbol, and logo after the expiration of 90 days via its letter of intent on Sept. 22. She sought a declaration that the establishment of INEC’s Fund pursuant to Section 3 (1) & (2) of the Electoral Act, 2022, upon which the totality of the expenditure of the commission is charged, and Section 75(6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which empowered INEC at its discretion to fix an administrative fee as a precondition for processing an application for registration of a political party, is unreasonable, unwarranted, unjustified and inconsistent with Section 4 (1) of the Electoral Act, 2022. She sought a declaration that the failure of INEC in responding to the letter of intent of the plaintiff was deemed to be a no objection to the name, symbol and acronym of the plaintiff’s association. She also sought a declaration that the provision of Section 75 (6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which provides for a separate source of funds in the form of a fee or levy on political associations for the performance of the constitutional function of registration of political parties, is inconsistent with Section 4 (1) (f) of the Electoral Act, 2022, and thus should be struck down by the court. Nwekeke further submitted that INEC’s failure in providing its account details to the plaintiff’s association for payment of the administrative fee was deemed to be a waiver and that it was meant to frustrate the application of the plaintiff’s association. She therefore prayed the court for an order directing the defendant to accept from the plaintiff’s association its application for registration as a political party. Besides, she sought a declaration that the application submitted pursuant to the relief above was proper. INEC, through its lawyer, Segun Bello, disagreed with the plaintiff’s submissions. The electoral umpire, in its counter affidavit, stated that the plaintiff’s letter of intent did not have a symbol of the party and that the general election is fixed for January 2027, which means that the court, granting the reliefs of the plaintiff, means that it would be required to file a formal application letter and it would be less than 12 months to the general election. The commission also submitted that the letter of intent written by the plaintiff’s association did not meet the requirements of the law, as it did not contain the symbol of the proposed political party, and thus it is void. It argued that since there was no valid letter of intent, the plaintiff’s association had no right to claim reliefs. INEC, therefore, urged the court to refuse the reliefs sought. Delivering the judgment, Justice Omotosho observed that from a cursory look at Section 3, especially Section 3 (2)(c), aids, grants or any other accruals are quite open-ended. “An accrual in accounting terms refers to revenues and expenses. “This means that revenues generated by the defendant can be paid into the Independent National Electoral Commission Fund. “The administrative fee being debated by the plaintiff is meant for the registration of political parties, and being a revenue accruing to the defendant, it can rightly be paid into the Fund. “Importantly, this also implies that the defendant is within its powers to demand administrative or processing fees, such as fees for the production and certification of the national voters register. “The fact that an institution receives funding from the Federation Account does not mean that it cannot generate funds or charge fees for some of its activities. “For instance, the judiciary receives funding from the Consolidated Revenue Fund; however, courts still fix filing fees and processing fees for court processes. “There is no express prohibition on the defendant to refrain from fixing administrative fees. “Consequently, I hold that the defendant has powers to fix administrative fees for the purpose of registration of political parties. “In final analysis, the claim of the plaintiff is without merit, and the suit has become academic. Consequently, the suit is hereby dismissed,” the judge ruled. (NAN) The post 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: How was a teacher facing sexual misconduct allegations promoted to headmaster? – Sarpong Asiedu questions GES
items.description: A Democracy and Development Fellow in Public Health at CDD-Ghana, Kwame Sarpong Asiedu, has questioned the circumstances under which the headmaster at the centre of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School sexual abuse allegations was appointed, amid claims of earlier misconduct. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, 2st1 October, he said allegations relating to the headmaster’s previous role as an assistant headmaster raised serious questions about safeguarding and oversight within the Ghana Education Service (GES). “If that was known, under what circumstances did this person get to be a headmaster?” he asked. The headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai was accused of sexual misconduct when he was an assistant headmaster in other school before becoming a headmaster in Obuasi SHTS. Mr Sarpong Asiedu argued that any investigation should examine whether earlier allegations were brought to the attention of education authorities and how they were handled before the appointment. He questioned whether giving greater authority to someone facing unresolved allegations could expose students to further harm. His comments came during a discussion on the ongoing Obuasi SHTS controversy and the GES’s response, including asking education directors to step aside and establishing another committee to investigate the sexual abuse allegations. Mr Sarpong Asiedu said the matter must be considered through the principles of duty of care and the responsibility school authorities assume when parents entrust children to them. He explained that education professionals are expected to safeguard students’ health, safety, dignity and welfare, including protecting them from sexual abuse. “That is, as a parent, if I bring my child to you to take care of them in a boarding house, I am devolving my responsibility as a parent to you, so you are acting in my stead,” he said. He stressed that these responsibilities extended beyond the headmaster to officials responsible for supervising the school and responding to complaints. According to him, investigators must establish whether those officials failed to protect staff tasked with safeguarding students or adequately address concerns brought before them. “Therefore, it is understandable that they will be asked to step aside because their complicity has to be investigated as well. Whether it was knowingly or unknowingly, it has to be investigated,” he said. Mr Sarpong Asiedu also expressed concern about what he described as a wider culture of protectionism surrounding people in authority who face sexual misconduct allegations. “So, you can see that this cloak of protectionism is wider both in the school and extra the school,” he said. Questioning whether the allegations would have received the same attention without the students’ protest, he called for scrutiny of the entire chain of responsibility. “And let’s ask ourselves, if that revolt hadn’t happened by the students, would we have been having this conversation?” he asked.

items.title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in alleged CCD encounter
items.description: The suspect accused of running over and fatally injuring a 14-year-old boy in Multan was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur early on Wednesday, police said. The suspect, identified as Tauqeer, had allegedly escaped from police custody while on remand, a CCD spokesperson said. A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of the suspect. The suspect was accused of hitting the victim, who used to work for him, with his car in a private housing society. He was arrested on Monday and presented before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam on Tuesday. According to the spokesperson, the CCD personnel attempted to stop two individuals riding a motorcycle on Bahawalpur’s Northern Bypass when an exchange of fire ensued, leaving the suspect dead. On Tuesday, police requested a 14-day physical remand of the suspect for investigation. However, the judicial magistrate granted the police a three-day remand. At the time, Multan City Police Officer (CPO) Akhtar Farooq said while speaking to the media that raids were being conducted for the arrest of a second suspect. “We all are in deep pain,” the CPO said, adding that the orphan boy had been “subjected to barbarity”. The CCTV footage of the incident shows a boy running on the road after spotting a car. The car is seen swerving and chasing the boy, eventually hitting him. The boy, who fell, then rams into the gate of a nearby house and dies on impact. A case was registered on the state’s behalf at Multan’s DHA police station. The first information report (FIR) named two suspects and invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. According to the FIR, the teenage boy had been working for the suspects and was being trained as an electrician. His cousin told police that the boy had reportedly faced violence and threats by the suspects, the FIR said, adding that the 14-year-old was fleeing when the suspects pursued him in a car and hit him. Police arrested one of the suspects while the other escaped, the FIR stated. It added that their vehicle had been taken into custody.

items.title: Macron takes aim at Trump for using France riots for election gain
items.description: President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday took an apparent swipe at counterpart Donald Trump of exploiting France’s riots for advantage in the US midterm election battle, as Paris prepared for more protests this weekend. Macron, speaking during a visit to Qatar, implied that Trump, and possibly Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is also in election mode , made “stupid comments” on the unrest for political gain, though he did not name either leader. “There are people who campaign at France’s expense — leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic,” he told reporters in Doha. Macron made his remarks as he and his government struggled to get on top of a crisis that has scarred France’s image both abroad and in financial markets, six months ahead of presidential elections to choose his successor. France’s government has admitted it “lost control” in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings. Trump has sought to link the “revolution” in France to “migrants, jihadists, and communists” as he campaigned for his Republican party in the United States on his anti-immigration messaging. He also on Tuesday hailed French far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who shares his ideologies, as a conservative voice, with surveys putting her as the frontrunner in France’s presidential race. Trump’s ally Netanyahu, facing his own tough election battle, on Tuesday argued that France had been hit by an “invasion of extremist Islam”. Several analysts have dismissed the claims that migrants were driving France’s protests. Curfews The unrest overshadowed demonstrations held on Saturday in which more than half a million people marched nationwide against the cost of living. Those rallies followed four weeks of student protests that have closed many schools across France. Since the rioting — the worst France has seen in years — and ahead of further cost-of-living demonstrations this coming Saturday, Macron’s government has warned it will brook no further violence. Authorities in Paris and several other cities imposed nighttime curfews Monday and Tuesday in certain zones prone to protests or looting. Macron said that on Thursday he would chair a meeting of key ministers and intelligence officials to receive a “detailed account” of what happened last weekend. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who on Wednesday held a meeting with union leaders organising marches, has vowed a “massive” police deployment for the fresh demonstrations called for Saturday by the Yellow Vest movement protesting rising inflation. The convulsion in France, the EU’s second-biggest economy after Germany, has rattled financial markets already nervous about the country’s growing debt pile and deficit. The yield on the French government’s benchmark 10-year bond has been rising, and on Wednesday surpassed five percent as investors demanded a higher return given the fiscal woes. A rising yield signifies a drop in bond prices. The Paris stock market also fell. On Friday, the Moody’s ratings agency is expected to lower its grade on France’s public debt. The country’s political landscape is so fragmented that Lecornu has little chance of winning swift parliamentary consensus for a cost-cutting budget that needs to be adopted before the end of this year. Le Pen leads race The latest survey, carried out by Ifop in the wake of the riots, suggested Le Pen would lead first-round voting intentions by a wide margin and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerged as her most likely opponent in the runoff. France’s neighbours Italy and Belgium have also started to experience similar unrest, on a smaller scale. Italy’s government has ordered 500 troops to Milan to stem street violence there. Macron said that “we don’t need a state of emergency” that would likewise permit soldiers to reinforce police against rioters, adding that “we have the means” already at authorities’ disposal, such as curfews. While the partial curfews have led to a calming of the situation in Paris and elsewhere, they have disrupted travel for commuters looking to take urban rail after 11pm (2am PKT). “It’s quite disconcerting,” said one Paris commuter who gave only his first name, Louis, when he found his line closed. But “if it can prevent further acts of vandalism… then yes, I think it’s a good thing”, he said. The Yellow Vest movement behind last weekend’s demonstrations announced on Wednesday that it had formally told authorities it planned to hold its Paris march on Saturday starting from Bastille square. The movement also wants to hold follow-up nationwide demonstrations on Nov 5. The images broadcast around the world of France’s street violence last weekend have prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.

items.title: Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France
items.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has been pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match, which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday, will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday, with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. PSG will host Lyon at the same venue in a Ligue 1 match on Sunday evening. AFP The post Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tivaouane Peulh–Niague : un centre commercial de deux milliards de FCfa inauguré
items.description: D'un coût global d'environ deux milliards de FCfa, le nouveau centre commercial « Tawfex » de Tivaouane Peulh–Niague a été officiellement réceptionné hier, mardi 20 octobre. Ce complexe marchand moderne marque une étape cruciale dans l'amélioration des conditions de travail des commerçants. La coordonnatrice nationale du Programme de modernisation et de gestion des marchés (Promogem), Rougui Aladji Sow, a procédé, hier, mardi 20 octobre, à la réception du centre commercial « Tawfex », sis à Tivaouane Peulh–Niague. Bâti sur 9.550 m², l’infrastructure offre, sur deux niveaux, des espaces commerciaux de nouvelle génération. Il est composé de 275 magasins, 40 toilettes, une salle de sport, un espace commercial pour la vente des fruits et légumes. A lire aussi : Réhabilitation de la route des Niayes: les riverains s’impatientent malgré un rythme des travaux jugé satisfaisant Estimé à près de deux milliards de FCfa, le centre dispose aussi de commodités modernes, notamment un bloc administratif, un espace de microfinance et une chambre froide. L’aboutissement de ce chantier marque une nouvelle étape pour le développement de l’économie locale. Selon Mme Sow, « cette infrastructure va améliorer les conditions de travail des commerçants, dynamiser le commerce local et participer favorablement au bien-être des populations locales ». Son érection est donc une réponse concrète à la modernisation des infrastructures marchandes. Cependant, la coordonnatrice nationale du Promogem a insisté sur la nécessité de l’entretenir. « Avec ce centre commercial moderne, nous traduisons la vision de l'État. Le défi actuel du Promogem n'est pas simplement de construire des murs et des bâtiments. Il s’agit de bâtir un véritable système de gestion qui garantira une gestion efficace, avec plus de sécurité et une bonne hygiène », a-t-elle souligné. Le maire de Tivaouane Peulh–Niague, Momar Sokhna Diop, a, pour sa part, magnifié le travail du Promogem qui, d’après lui, permet de transformer radicalement les espaces commerciaux. En plus de veiller à l’entretien de cet ouvrage, l’édile a exprimé la volonté de la municipalité de développer une bonne politique de suivi afin de garantir la durabilité de l’édifice. « Aujourd’hui, nous disposons d'un magnifique centre commercial et il nous incombe de le maintenir en parfait état pour le bien-être des populations. Le modèle de gestion choisi par le Promogem pour cette infrastructure nous convient pleinement et, ensemble, nous relèverons ces défis », a fait savoir le maire. Bada MBATHIE

items.title: Transavia et Volotea réduisent la voilure, Air Algérie passe à l’offensive
items.description: Après Transavia, la compagnie Volotea réduit discrètement sa voiture vers l’Algérie à partir de villes françaises pour la saison hivernale. Une aubaine pour Air Algérie qui renforce sa position sur le marché très lucratif des liaisons Algérie-France, et dans le même temps, elle lance une nouvelle offensive commerciale. La faible demande en saison hivernale et la hausse des coûts de kérosène incitent les compagnies aériennes à revoir la fréquence de leurs vols. La compagnie espagnole à bas prix Volotea a revu à la baisse son offre hivernale qui passe de 25 395 à 17 048 vols et de 4 362 216 à 2 915 028 sièges, rapporte le site spécialisé aeroroutes.com . Volotea réduit la fréquence de ses vols entre la France et l’Algérie Cette baisse de l’offre concerne plusieurs liaisons vers l’Algérie. La même source indique que le service Marseille-Béjaïa est annulé pour la période du 5 janvier au 18 février, Bordeaux-Oran est réduit de 63 à 44 vols, Lyon-Sétif de 97 à 86 vols, Marseille-Alger de 308 à 294, Marseille-Constantine de 75 à 66, Marseille-Oran de 254 à 139 et Marseille-Tlemcen de 20 à 17 vols. Enfin, le service Limoges – Oran est prolongé pendant la saison hivernale, avec un vol hebdomadaire aux dates suivantes : du 21 octobre 2026 au 6 janvier 2027 et du 18 février 2027 au 25 mars 2027. Transavia avait réduit ses vols de Montpellier vers Alger et Oran En septembre dernier, la compagnie néerlandaise Transavia a réduit sa voilure vers l’Algérie au départ de Montpellier à cause de la hausse des prix du kérosène. Sur la ligne Montpellier – Alger, Transavia ne propose que 4 vols pour ce mois d’octobre, 3 vols pour novembre, 3 vols pour décembre, 5 vols pour janvier 2027, 4 vols pour février 2027 et 3 vols pour mars 2027. Sur la liaison Montpellier – Oran, il est programmé un seul vol en octobre, 5 vols en novembre, 4 vols en décembre, 5 vols en janvier, 4 en février et 3 vols en mars 2027. Air Algérie lance sa promotion d’automne … Pendant que ces compagnies low-cost réduisent la fréquence de leurs vols, Air Algérie maintient tous ses programmes. La compagnie algérienne passe même à l’offensive avec le lancement de sa promotion spécial automne, prévoyant des réductions allant jusqu'à 50% sur les lignes internationales. La promotion a été lancée lundi 19 octobre. “L'automne vous réserve des offres exceptionnelles. Profitez de réductions allant jusqu'à 50 % sur les vols internationaux avec Air Algérie et faites de votre prochaine destination l'occasion de découvrir de nouveaux horizons”, a écrit la compagnie nationale sur ses réseaux sociaux. Air Algérie ouvre 6 nouvelles lignes en une semaine Air Algérie poursuit aussi l'extension de ses dessertes internationales et s’apprête à ouvrir six nouvelles lignes. Selon le site Air Plus News, la compagnie aérienne algérienne lancera à partir du 25 octobre les lignes Alger–Conakry avec une fréquence de 3 vols par semaine, Alger–Brazzaville (3 vols hebdomadaires), Alger–Lagos–Abuja (1 vol hebdomadaire), Alger–Shanghai (3 vols/semaine en A330-900neo), Alger–Koweït–Amman (1 vol/semaine) ainsi que la reprise de la fréquence quotidienne Alger–Doha après 7 mois d’interruption. L’article Transavia et Volotea réduisent la voilure, Air Algérie passe à l’offensive est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Achraf Hakimi prévient l’Europe : le PSG veut conserver sa couronne continentale
items.description: Après le succès du Paris Saint-Germain face au FC Barcelone (4-2) en Ligue des champions, Achraf Hakimi a réaffirmé les ambitions du club parisien. Le latéral marocain estime que son équipe a les moyens de continuer à dominer l’Europe et vise un troisième sacre consécutif dans la compétition. Le Paris Saint-Germain a envoyé un signal fort à ses concurrents européens. Vainqueurs du FC Barcelone sur le score de 4-2, mardi soir au Parc des Princes, les Parisiens ont signé une nouvelle performance de référence après avoir également pris le dessus sur Manchester City une semaine auparavant. À l’issue de cette rencontre spectaculaire, Achraf Hakimi n’a pas caché sa satisfaction. Pour l’international marocain, ce succès illustre la capacité du PSG à répondre présent face aux grandes équipes européennes et à assumer son statut de champion. « Nous voulons montrer que nous sommes les champions et que nous voulons continuer à gagner » , a expliqué le défenseur parisien, qui considère son équipe comme l’une des meilleures du monde actuellement. Face à un FC Barcelone jusque-là invaincu cette saison, les joueurs de Luis Enrique ont dû faire preuve de caractère. Malgré les égalisations catalanes et les difficultés rencontrées au cours du match, le PSG a su trouver les ressources nécessaires pour faire la différence. Hakimi a notamment insisté sur l’intensité exigée par ce type de confrontation, où la rigueur défensive compte autant que la capacité à se montrer dangereux en attaque. Il a également salué la qualité de l’adversaire, tout en soulignant la force collective de son équipe. Pour le Marocain, cette victoire ne constitue pas une fin en soi. Le club parisien entend poursuivre sur cette lancée et défendre son titre européen avec une ambition clairement affichée. Le latéral du PSG a également évoqué l’objectif majeur de la saison : remporter une nouvelle Ligue des champions. Après deux sacres consécutifs, les Parisiens veulent prolonger leur règne continental et inscrire un peu plus leur nom dans l’histoire de la compétition. Hakimi attribue une partie de cette ambition au travail quotidien de Luis Enrique, qui veille à entretenir l’état d’esprit conquérant de son groupe. Selon lui, le technicien espagnol pousse ses joueurs à maintenir un niveau d’exigence élevé et à ne jamais se satisfaire des résultats déjà obtenus. items.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Cross River State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, endorsing the proposed establishment of state police to address insecurity through a decentralised policing system. All 22 lawmakers present at plenary voted in favour of the bill, with none opposing it. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. Ayambem, however, stressed that the implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, said policing must be brought closer to the people. He argued that a decentralised system would improve security responses and enable law enforcement agencies to address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies to ensure that the proposed State Police Services complemented existing security structures and improved overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, emphasised the need for adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism in the proposed system. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect citizens’ fundamental rights. Lawmakers also identified improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as potential benefits of decentralised policing. The passage marks the Cross River Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional amendments. The bill must proceed through the constitutionally prescribed amendment process before the proposed changes can take effect nationally. items.title: Egypt Forum 2026 celebrates higher attendance at schools still struggling without teachers or classrooms
items.description: Education has remained one of the main domestic fronts for the government in recent years, with chronic complaints around low spending in the sector. At the start of the academic year in September, Education Minister Mohamed Abdel Latif faced fierce public and parliamentary pushback over controversial decisions affecting schools nationwide. Chief among them was the new enforcement of compulsory weekly assessments and homework, along with curriculum shakeups that drew formal parliamentary briefing requests accusing the ministry of running an evaluation regime that burns out students and teachers — who are already scarce — without improving learning. Amid this simmering backlash, the Cabinet scrambled to stage-manage the narrative ahead of Egypt Forum 2026, a multi-day event mandated by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on October 1 to showcase national development and institutional dialogue. After opening a window for people to register questions and concerns for discussion at the forum, the Cabinet said that education had outpaced all other issues with more than 15,000 public inquiries submitted on the topic, reflecting the degree of public concern. We don’t know what these public inquiries were, as they have not been published in a publicly accessible location so far. So, what did the government choose to talk about? In line with the presidency’s official “ human development ” agenda, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly announced earlier this month that basic education would anchor the forum’s flagship opening session under the title: “What Do Our Children Learn… and Does It Prepare Them for the Future?” Decision-makers and policy experts at the forum framed a discussion of education policy around the central question of whether current curricula adequately prepare students for future labor market demands. But after the display of a video on education “ challenges and achievements ” which Mada Masr was not able to review, the forum proceeded on Monday with the minister outlining a set of achievements leading with huge improvements in school attendance — a fact presented as a fait accompli that would allow the government’s policy focus to transition “from expanding basic school access, to ensuring actual learning quality,” as one of the session aims stated. Mada Masr looked into the claim that school attendance and access has improved enough to allow for improvements to learning quality, exploring government data and statements, and speaking with the education program coordinator at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights. What we found is that at least part of the boost in attendance is driven by the most recent curriculum change: increased regular testing, which is an innovation that the government says is improving learning, despite complaints about the approach from families and MPs who say it increases the strain on teachers and students without improving educational outcomes, as well as conflicting with recommended educational approaches in pedagogical research. We also looked into the government’s ambitious target to improve learning by reducing classroom density and canceling school “evening shifts,” finding that these aims will be difficult to implement without radical changes to how it is currently handling the major deficit in classroom provision and teacher hiring. *** Speaking at the forum on Monday, the education minister laid out numbers to demonstrate improvements in the last decade to children’s access to government schools — attended by 80 percent of Egyptian pupils. Abdel Latif said attendance rates stood at just 15 percent in the 2023/24 academic year, but have risen exponentially to reach 87 percent for the following school year. The dramatic improvement was celebrated in May by the head of education at UNICEF Egypt, Shiraz Chakera, who cited a new study on Egypt’s educational reforms from 2024 to 2026 in a conference with the government. And the number is still going up, the minister asserted at the forum, saying the attendance rate has risen from 87 percent to 90 percent for the current school year. These figures appear positive. But they don’t tell us who is attending school and why. Mada Masr looked into the numbers to understand if the higher attendance represents real improvement across pre-university education, and tried to understand where the change has come from and whether it indicates a strong base for the curriculum reforms the government is looking to focus on. Regular testing keeps pupils in school, but is it improving learning? High attendance in the primary and preparatory stages is not new. In 2021, 93 percent of children aged 6 to 11 were already attending school, and only 3.4 per cent of primary school age children were “out-of-school,” or 3.6 per cent of preparatory school age children, according to the Egyptian Family Health Survey, whose data was cited by UNICEF in a 2024 report. Attendance has historically been less strong for secondary school age children. The same study put the percentage of children of secondary school age who don’t go to school at almost four times higher than at primary school age, at 12.2 per cent, or around 1.4 million children. But in general, head of the education program at EIPR Mohamed Sayed agreed that there is a marked improvement in primary and secondary school attendance. Speaking to Mada Masr, the researcher put improved attendance down, in part, to the compulsory regular testing that has been introduced alongside the new Egyptian Baccalaureate program launched this year as an alternative to the traditional thanaweya amma Through the program, the Education Ministry has codified regular assessments into high school graduation requirements. Education Ministerial Decree 150/2026, published in the Official Gazette on October 15, says that Egyptian Baccalaureate students must get at least 60 percent on weekly and monthly evaluations in each subject to be eligible to take graduation exams in their last two years of secondary school. Sayed noted that while the exams may have supported a boost in secondary school attendance, the regular testing is something that parents and teachers have complained places children and teachers under undue stress. Abdel Latif further defended on Monday the weekly assessments, homework and monthly tests as essential tools used internationally to monitor student understanding, citing their global adoption to justify the policy. But the system has faced domestic pushback, with critics arguing that it fails to improve learning outcomes while placing an undue burden on both students and teachers. In the days leading up to the forum, two MPs filed separate parliamentary briefing requests about intensive testing in school curricula. MP Nashwa al-Sherif said students should have enough time to understand and review their lessons without being under constant pressure over grades, according to news reports, while MP Amal Asfour said that tying grades to attendance, or using assessments as a means of disciplining or pressuring children, could negatively affect their relationship with school. Modern international educational trends have also increasingly shifted away from excessive testing, favoring approaches that afford teachers and students greater flexibility to focus on deep learning. For instance, a prominent semi-national language school in downtown Cairo recently held a back-to-school orientation where the pedagogical team emphasized a reduced-testing philosophy in meeting notes distributed to parents and reviewed by Mada Masr . According to the meeting notes, the French curriculum for the French Baccalaureat operates on multi-year learning cycles rather than a strict annual framework, relying on continuous assessment to track progress instead of high-stakes examinations that place pressure on students. The pedagogical focus is on skills, contrasting with the traditional system’s emphasis on rote knowledge and uniform teaching methods. The international track also embeds the “right to make mistakes” and encourages progressive student autonomy under less directive supervision, allowing grade advancement within cycles without mandatory end-of-year exams. Attendance growth outstrips classroom capacity With the improved school attendance relying on extensive testing, schools which were already struggling with few classrooms and even fewer teachers now have a greater number of pupils and extra workload for teachers to grapple with. The minister’s focus on increased attendance glossed over the compounding deficits in the number of classrooms and in teaching capacity that are documented in the government’s own records. He estimated in 2024 a shortfall of about 250,000 classrooms, resulting in serious classroom overcrowding. “Some of the classrooms had 100 or 150 students,” he said during the forum, citing Al-Marg and Khanka as some examples. But now, “there isn’t a class with over 50 students in it,” he claimed, adding that in future, “we have a vision to reduce the density to 40 and 45 students in one classr oom.” How can the ministry achieve this ambition? So far, its rate of classroom building has been much slower than what is needed to reduce classroom density in a meaningful way, based on the figures Mada Masr reviewed. According to publicly available data in the ministry’s ‘ yearbook ,’ there were 435,308 government school classrooms during the 2019/20 academic year. This number increased to 591,217 classes for the academic year 2024/25. As per Mada Masr’s calculations, based on the ministry’s data over that period, the increase in the number of government school classrooms happened as follows: 6,477 new classrooms were added in the 2020/21 academic year 16,115 in 2021/22 5,271 in 2022/23 777 in 2023/24 127,269 in 2024/25 But not all of these classrooms represent newly built additions. The minister said on Monday that 150,000 new classrooms have been added over the past ten years at a cost exceeding LE200 billion. The ministry spokesperson has also said in recent months that since Adbel Latif became minister, 98,000 of the new classrooms have come from “introducing” new school rooms for use in classes. This has relied on re-utilizing existing rooms in schools, the spokesperson explained, alongside the policy to reduce classroom density by splitting classroom use between evening and morning school “shifts.” But now, alongside the ambitious target to reduce classroom density down to 40-45 students, the minister also announced on Monday a major target to stop running school evening shifts by 2029. How the government aims to both reduce classroom density and end the evening shifts with no plan to increase the number of available rooms is unclear. Abdel Latif announced no additional spending plan to build new classrooms in line with the plan to cancel the evening shifts. Discounting the 98,000 “introduced” clasrooms from the figures on classroom additions for the past five years, the figures show an average increase in school classrooms of around 11,581 classrooms per year over the past five years. At this average rate of government classroom addition per year, it would take over 10 years to plug the gap of 250,000 missing classrooms identified by the ministry in 2024, even if we subtract from the target the classrooms added in the 2024/25 academic year, including the 98,000 reutilized classrooms. And teachers are still left at the bottom of the barrel As well as no policy plan to increase classrooms, Abdel Latif also neglected to announce how the government will address the urgent teachers shortage. Teachers are one of the main victims of the Education Ministry’s unwillingness to spend on its policies. With strict regulations on hiring in the public sector, the ministry has acknowledged the huge gap in the number of teachers available. Abdel Latif pointed to the ongoing deficit on Monday, saying that the public education system faces an estimated deficit of more than 469,000 teachers, with a current teaching force of 832,000. Still, hiring remains limited to around 30,000 teachers per year on the basis of annual “competitions” that slowly rule out applicants based on criteria including physical fitness and weight, as Mada Masr documented in 2022. One of the applicants said at the time that they had “passed all the tests related to academic and educational specialization, general culture, computer use and proficiency in English,” but had failed a round of physical testing hosted at the Military Academy where their height and weight were recorded, and they were asked to do push ups, sit ups and jumps. High competition for positions and frustration with the weight-based discrimination saw hundreds of teachers protest the ministry’s hiring decisions at the end of the competition. Additional hiring competitions, launched last year, seek to offer assistant teacher contracts to teachers currently working per-class. 11,693 appointments were advertised last year, with a new initiative this year to hire the per-class teachers. But if the number of teachers hired per year remains around 40,000 — between granting contracts to per-class teachers and the hiring competitions — it will take the government 11 years to fill the 469,000 positions that Abdel Latif said are needed *** This report is published as part of the joint campaign with eight media platforms in solidarity with the detained Matsda2sh journalists. The post Egypt Forum 2026 celebrates higher attendance at schools still struggling without teachers or classrooms first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Man arrested after allegedly taping wife to chair to watch football ‘in peace’
items.description: A 64-year-old Richmond man is facing serious legal consequences after he reportedly bound his wife to a chair with tape and left her in their basement so he could watch a football game upstairs without interruption. The suspect, identified as Terry Ward, was taken into custody following a late-night domestic disturbance call at a residence in the 2200 block of Maplewood Avenue in Richmond. According to a Richmond Police Department criminal complaint obtained by Virginia Statewide Incidents, officers arrived at the scene around 11:30 p.m. to investigate a domestic dispute. Responding officers took a statement from an adult female who detailed a harrowing 30 to 45-minute ordeal. She told investigators that her husband had forcibly restrained her to a chair in the basement using tape. The responding officer noted in the complaint that the physical evidence heavily backed her claim, documenting visible marks and sticky tape residue around both of the woman’s arms. According to the official court documents, investigators secured an outright admission from the suspect at the scene. The officer explicitly wrote in the criminal complaint that Ward stated he “did indeed tie his wife to a chair and place her down in the basement.” Sources familiar with the case confirmed that while his wife remained trapped downstairs, Ward went back upstairs to watch the game in complete isolation. Following the police response, Ward was arrested and formally charged with felony abduction and misdemeanour assault on a family member. Online records from the Richmond Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court indicate that his next formal court appearance is scheduled for November 10, 2026. The post Man arrested after allegedly taping wife to chair to watch football ‘in peace’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Monrovia set for AWBL Zone 3 qualifying showdown
items.description: The race for two places in the final rounds of the African Women’s Basketball League (AWBL) will take centre stage in Monrovia, Liberia as six clubs prepare to compete in the FIBA Africa Zone 3 qualifiers from November 2 to 9, 2026. With the competition set for the Samuel Kanyon Doe (SKD) Indoor Gymnasium in Paynesville, the participating teams face a demanding week in which every result could prove decisive in their quest to reach the continental finals in Cairo, Egypt, scheduled for December 11–19. Liberia will have two representatives in the contest, with Flames Basketball Club, the domestic league runners-up, joined by reigning national champions D’Rockers Basketball Club. Both sides will be eager to make home advantage count against a competitive field. Côte d’Ivoire’s Friends of Basketball Association (FBA), the defending FIBA Africa Zone 3 champions, will arrive with a title to defend, while Benin Republic’s Energie Basketball Club of Cotonou brings its experience from previous appearances in the competition. Nigeria’s Mountain of Fire Ministries (MFM) Basketball Club and First Bank Basketball Club complete the six-team lineup, setting up another chapter in one of the country’s notable domestic rivalries. MFM heads to Liberia with bragging rights after edging First Bank 66–64 in the Zenith Bank Women’s Basketball League final at the Indoor Sports Hall of the National Stadium. The closely fought encounter, played before a packed arena, underlined how little separates the two Nigerian sides. Their meeting in Monrovia could therefore carry added significance, as both clubs seek to translate their domestic form into continental success and secure passage to Cairo. The Nigerian representatives were able to enter the qualifiers after FIBA Africa and the Liberia Basketball Association (LBA) extended the registration deadline and adjusted the competition schedule. The changes followed an intervention by FIBA Africa Zone 3 President, Colonel Sam Ahmedu (Rtd), enabling both clubs to participate after the late conclusion of their domestic league campaign. Preparations in Liberia are also gathering momentum. Calvin Diggs, president of Flames Basketball Club and Secretary-General of the LBA, told FIRST ZEALMEDIACAST BLOG in a telephone interview from Monrovia that they are working to ensure a smooth and successful event. According to Diggs, the Organizing Committee and the LBA have intensified preparations, with the goal of delivering a competition that meets international standards. FIBA Africa Zone 3 Secretary Joe Apu also expressed confidence in Liberia’s readiness, pointing to the experience accumulated by the country’s basketball community through hosting several international events in recent years. As the countdown continues, the six clubs are reportedly reinforcing their squads ahead of the showdown. The immediate objective for the teams are clear, finish among the top two and earn the opportunity to compete for the AWBL title in Egypt. With the defending zonal champions, two Nigerian rivals, experienced Beninese contenders and a determined Liberian challenge all in the mix, the Monrovia qualifiers promise a compelling test of depth, consistency and ambition.

items.title: Dix suspects interpellés dans une affaire présumée de réseau QNET
items.description: La Brigade territoriale de Sangalkam a interpellé dix ressortissants étrangers, le lundi 19 octobre 2026, à Kounoune Centrale, au Sénégal, à la suite d’un renseignement signalant la présence présumée d’un réseau lié à QNET. Les investigations se poursuivent pour déterminer l’étendue des activités de ce réseau et établir les responsabilités des personnes mises en cause. L’opération menée par la Brigade territoriale de Sangalkam a conduit à l’arrestation de dix individus de différentes nationalités. Parmi les personnes interpellées figurent sept ressortissants guinéens, deux Ivoiriennes et une Burkinabè. Cette intervention fait suite à des informations faisant état de l’existence présumée d’un réseau QNET dans la localité de Kounoune Centrale. Après leur interpellation, les dix suspects ont été conduits dans les locaux de l’unité de gendarmerie pour les besoins de l’enquête. Les investigations se poursuivent afin de faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire, notamment en déterminant l’ampleur des activités du réseau présumé et le degré d’implication de chacun des mis en cause. items.title: Football guinéen : le candidat Ibrahima Kalil Kaba dresse un constat préoccupant après sa tournée à l’intérieur du pays
items.description: À quelques jours de l’élection du nouveau bureau exécutif de la Fédération guinéenne de football (FGF), prévue le 27 octobre 2026, le candidat Ibrahima Kalil Kaba, dit « Lilou », a effectué une tournée à l’intérieur du pays. Cette démarche lui a permis de rencontrer et d’échanger avec les acteurs du football à la base. Dans cet entretien accordé au service des sports de la RTG, le candidat revient sur les différentes étapes de cette tournée ainsi que sur les échanges avec les acteurs du football guinéen. Lisez ! Question : Vous rentrez d’une longue tournée à travers le pays. Vous êtes parti vendre quoi à la famille du football ? Ibrahima Kalil Kaba : Ce que nous sommes partis vendre, c’est essentiellement le programme de société de notre liste CAP 20-30. Nous avons décidé, avec d’autres acteurs du football, des hommes et des femmes qui vivent et respirent le football guinéen, de présenter une liste, non pas dans une démarche de promotion personnelle, mais plutôt dans une démarche collective, pour essayer de faire face aux maux qui, selon nous, minent notre football national et apporter des solutions. Si nous allons solliciter un mandat électif en tant que membres de la Fédération, il nous paraissait tout à fait logique d’aller vers ces membres avec ce programme, d’échanger avec eux et, peut-être, de recueillir des idées que nous n’avions pas eues lors de son élaboration. Nous sommes donc partis aux quatre coins de la Guinée et nous sommes rentrés il y a deux jours. Question : Par rapport à cette tournée, quelle a été la préoccupation majeure des acteurs que vous avez rencontrés à l’intérieur du pays ? Ibrahima Kalil Kaba : Je crois que, s’il faut parler d’une préoccupation majeure, c’est peut-être la désunion. C’était très frappant. Partout où nous sommes passés, nous avons constaté un rejet collectif de toutes ces bisbilles autour du football qui, à mon sens, et c’est peut-être aussi l’avis des membres, sont devenues un véritable facteur d’asphyxie. C’était très clair et cela s’est exprimé partout. Sur tous les sujets abordés, nous avons senti que les acteurs étaient un peu fatigués des guerres, surtout des conflits entre personnes. Donc, si l’on doit parler d’une préoccupation majeure, je crois que c’est celle qui revient chez les uns et les autres. Question : Quels enseignements avez-vous tirés après avoir écouté les acteurs à Labé, Kindia, Kankan et N’Zérékoré ? Et comment voyez-vous le football guinéen ? Ibrahima Kalil Kaba : Le premier enseignement, c’est que nous ne nous portons pas bien. Et quand je dis que nous ne nous portons pas bien, je parle essentiellement du football. Sur le plan de la gouvernance, nous sommes confrontés à une succession de crises depuis une décennie. Nous avons connu deux CONOR, une assemblée générale n’a pas pu se tenir faute de quorum, un président élu a été destitué et un comité exécutif (COMEX) vient de démissionner. Tout cela en dix ans. Alors, comment pouvons-nous nous porter sur le plan de la gouvernance ? Nous sommes déjà dans une situation de crise permanente. En ce qui concerne les infrastructures, nous rencontrons des difficultés bien connues, notamment au niveau des grands stades. Certains ne sont pas en bon état, tandis que d’autres souffrent de problèmes d’entretien, en particulier au niveau des pelouses et des infrastructures associées. Il y a ensuite la question de la formation, qui a également été largement évoquée partout. Les besoins en formation sont criants, non seulement au sein des deux grandes corporations que sont les arbitres et les entraîneurs, mais aussi chez les administrateurs du football, les responsables de ligues, les secrétaires généraux de clubs, les team managers et les intendants. En grande partie, tout le monde parle de formation. Enfin, il y a la question des compétitions. Nous ne participons pas à suffisamment de compétitions formelles. Il existe beaucoup de compétitions informelles, mais elles ne sont pas organisées. Alors, comment nous portons-nous ? Je dirais que nous sommes malades. Propos décryptés par Youssouf Keita. items.title: IR : trois tranches et un taux plafonné à 30 % d’ici 2031
items.description: Seuil d’exonération porté à 60 000 DH par an, barème ramené de cinq à trois tranches, taux marginal abaissé de 37 à 30 % : le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031 détaille sa réforme de l’impôt sur le revenu, qui sera déployée progressivement entre 2027 et 2031. Dans un contexte de hausse continue du coût de la vie, le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031 fait de l’impôt sur le revenu (IR) l’un des leviers de la restauration du pouvoir d’achat. La réforme figure à la page 58, au premier axe, intitulé « Restauration du pouvoir d’achat », de l’Axe 4 du document, consacré à ce même pouvoir d’achat et à la consolidation de l’État social. Elle se veut progressive et poursuit trois objectifs : alléger la charge fiscale pesant sur les salariés et la classe moyenne, simplifier le barème et encourager l’emploi déclaré. La première mesure concerne le seuil d’exonération. Le programme prévoit de relever la première tranche, celle du revenu net exonéré d’impôt, de 40 000 à 60 000 DH par an, soit un relèvement de 20 000 DH du plafond annuel exonéré. Concrètement, les salariés dont le revenu net n’excède pas 5 000 DH par mois ne seraient plus imposés. Le barème lui-même change de forme. Le nombre de tranches d’imposition passerait de cinq à trois, assorties de taux progressifs de 10 %, 20 % et 30 %. Cette refonte vise à rendre l’impôt plus lisible pour les contribuables, en remplaçant une structure jugée complexe par une grille resserrée. La réforme touche également le sommet du barème. Le taux marginal appliqué à la dernière tranche, celle des revenus les plus élevés, serait ramené de 37 à 30 %, soit une baisse de sept points. Associé au relèvement du seuil d’exonération, cet allègement doit réduire la pression fiscale sur les salariés et la classe moyenne, comme l’affiche l’objectif principal de la réforme. Ce dispositif se distingue de ce que proposait le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) durant la campagne des législatives. Dans son programme électoral, dévoilé le 1er septembre à Rabat, le parti proposait de ramener le barème de six à trois tranches et d’abaisser le taux marginal maximal de 37 à 20 %, soit dix points de moins que le taux de 30 % retenu par le Programme gouvernemental. Le texte prévoyait un taux nul pour les salaires bruts inférieurs à 15 000 DH, de 10 % entre 15 000 et 46 000 DH, puis de 20 % au-delà. L’exonération visait ainsi les rémunérations brutes allant jusqu’à 15 000 DH, soit environ 12 500 DH nets. À titre de comparaison, le programme gouvernemental retient une exonération de 60 000 DH nets par an, soit 5 000 DH par mois, et un taux marginal de 30 %. La promesse électorale avait d’ailleurs suscité des interrogations sur son financement, son coût pour les finances publiques pouvant se chiffrer en dizaines de milliards de dirhams. Le programme gouvernemental s’attache précisément à cet équilibre budgétaire. La réforme de l’IR sera déployée progressivement sur cinq ans, de 2027 à 2031, après évaluation de son coût financier et de ses impacts sur les revenus des ménages comme sur les recettes publiques. The post IR : trois tranches et un taux plafonné à 30 % d’ici 2031 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: Police warn politicians against inflammatory speeches during campaigns
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor The Commissioner of Police in Rivers State, Olugbenga Adepoju, has tasked political parties and their candidates for the 2027 elections to engage in issue-based campaigns and shun inflammatory rhetoric. This was as stakeholders, including party leaders, traditional rulers and civil society organisations, have called on political actors. security agencies and citizens to embrace peaceful conduct before, during and after the 2027 general elections. These calls formed the major discussions of the one-day Rivers Dialogue, organised by the newsroom of Megalectrics Limited, operators of Beat FM, Classic FM and Naija FM, in collaboration with the Professor Oke Onuchuku Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies, Ignatius Ajuru University of Education, Port Harcourt. The dialogue, themed “Peaceful Elections: Sustainable Path for Economic Development,” brought together political actors, traditional rulers and other stakeholders to discuss ways to prevent electoral violence and strengthen democracy in the 2027 polls. Addressing the participants, Adepoju said peaceful elections were necessary to sustain investors’ confidence, protect businesses and create an environment for development. Adepoju, who was represented by the Assistant Commissioner of Police (Operations) for the Rivers State Police Command, Ikechukwu Okoro, urged political parties to discourage violence among their supporters and advised candidates to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than inflammatory rhetoric. He further called on the media to use their platforms responsibly to promote peace rather than escalate tensions during the election. Meanwhile, Head of News Department, Megaletrics, Allwell Ene, said the dialogue was put together to ensure a violence free election in the state. He said: “The Rivers Dialogue was designed towards fostering violence-free and peaceful elections in Rivers State come 2027. Elections are critical periods in Nigeria because they alter the power structure within a state, the sub-national and the national levels where known political actors seek to establish their claims to power.” Ene noted that the state is notorious for electoral violence and security breaches during elections in the country, adding that such violence spills into other elections which subsequently paralyses governance and economic activities in the state; hence, the dialogue intends to address some of the issues. Also speaking, the Director-General of the National Orientation Agency, Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, said credible elections required the collective responsibility of citizens, political institutions and electoral stakeholders. Issa-Onilu, represented by the Rivers State Director of NOA, Dr Banigo Edward, said the increasing number of registered voters alone could not guarantee credible elections without civic discipline, active participation and responsible conduct before, during and after the polls. He said: “A free, fair and credible election in 2027 cannot be guaranteed by INEC alone. It requires a collective responsibility, civic discipline, moral courage and active participation of every citizen.” However, the Paramount Ruler of Elelenwo Etor Kingdom in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of the state, His Royal Highness, Eze Sunny Weli Chukwu, called for proper training and orientation for security personnel deployed for election monitoring to prevent unnecessary violence. Chukwu urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure eligible voters had access to their Permanent Voter Cards and called on traditional rulers to educate their communities, particularly youths, against electoral violence and vote-buying. Meanwhile, the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Rivers State, Hon. Kingsley Ogundu Chinda, pledged his commitment to peaceful elections and governance, emphasising that protecting lives and property remained the primary responsibility of government. He said, “I am fully, unconditionally committed to a peaceful election and peaceful governance in Rivers State.” Other governorship candidates, including those of the Social Democratic Party and the Peoples Redemption Party, National Rescue Movement as well as Boot, also expressed their commitment to non-violent elections in the state. The post 2027: Police warn politicians against inflammatory speeches during campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: This Is Not a Cycle of Retribution
items.description: Donald Trump has spent nearly two years investigating, suing, or prosecuting anybody in politics, media, or government who ever defied him. Now, with Democrats poised to win control of one or both chambers of Congress, the administration and its allies are prepared to slip back into their familiar pose of victimhood. The putative evidence of imminent GOP persecution comes from Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who recently told the Vox journalist Astead Herndon during an event at the University of Chicago that Democrats should pursue accountability for the administration to, among other goals, deter new graduates from enlisting in corrupt schemes. “I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration?’” she said. “I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want, and so let me avoid participating in that.’” Slotkin made these remarks last Tuesday, attracting little notice at the time because she didn’t say anything particularly noteworthy. Five days later, a tidal wave of conservative outrage suddenly crashed over her. The Republican response has been revealing. Even Trump-skeptical conservatives are signaling that, just as they have in the past, his party will rally behind him the moment someone proposes that the laws of the country should be enforced if Trump is found to have engaged in misconduct. He has trained members of his party to sublimate any concern they may have about his actions beneath their partisan instincts. However queasy Trump might occasionally make them, they will return to his side the moment he faces the prospect of legal consequences. [ From the October 2026 issue: MAGA is making the world safe for corruption ] “It is absolutely disgraceful to threaten young Americans for participating in politics and serving their country,” Senator Mike Lee, a Utah Republican, complained . “This type of thinking is terrible for our country,” Ari Fleischer, the former press secretary to President George W. Bush, chimed in . Columns by the Trump legal adviser Mike Davis in Fox News and the writer Miranda Devine in the New York Post depict Slotkin as a goon who was menacing bright-eyed youth for no reason other than their partisan affiliation. “Slotkin is a lowlife who’s ruining her state,” Trump said in front of the White House when prodded for a reaction by a reporter. Trump went even further, as is his wont. “That’s a hell of a statement,” he told reporters. “Slotkin said that there should be prosecutions in order to scare people from going into politics.” In point of fact, Slotkin didn’t say anything about prosecutions. She was discussing congressional oversight and specifically describing a scenario in which Democrats had control of Congress but not the executive branch. She was arguing for a measured and focused approach, prioritizing only the most blatant forms of corruption. “We do have to have accountability for the unbelievable corruption that we are living under right now,” she said. “But you can’t just make that your whole personality. So you have to pick signature cases, and you have to go after people and projects that are just super egregious.” Later in the conversation, Herndon noted that Trump has largely insulated himself from accountability by stacking the courts and installing loyalists throughout his party and the federal government. That’s when Slotkin pointed out that exposing the administration’s corruption might deter ambitious Republicans from joining the administration during its final years. The outraged responses omitted the first part of Slotkin’s remarks, which point out the need to investigate the administration’s pervasive misconduct. Out of context, it sounds as if Slotkin is threatening young Republicans because of malevolence. But in context, her comments are understandable, even generous. If you knew a young person who had been planning to go to work for Elizabeth Holmes, deterring them by exposing the Theranos founder as a con artist would have been doing them a favor. Pretending that the Trump administration is innocent is just the first line of defense. The fallback argument against investigating, and perhaps eventually prosecuting, any corruption is that doing so will set off a cycle of retribution. A Wall Street Journal editorial accuses Slotkin of “essentially promising a scorched-earth lawfare campaign” that will invite reprisals. “This is where the multiple prosecutions that Democrats unleashed against Mr. Trump in the Biden years are taking us. Mr. Trump is retaliating with similar attempts to criminalize political differences. And now Ms. Slotkin is vowing more of the same. Down this road lies more bitterness and political dysfunction,” the Journal editorial laments. Jack Goldsmith, a former Bush-administration legal adviser, makes a similar argument in a Substack column . The fear that the two parties are locked in a cycle of retribution has a certain high-minded but superficial appeal. It’s true that Trump faced investigations after leaving office, and that he has cited these investigations as a rationale for his reign of legal terror. But Joe Biden did not behave in a remotely similar fashion. He appointed an attorney general, Merrick Garland, who commanded bipartisan respect. Garland operated cautiously, following traditional procedure, and appointed Jack Smith as a special counsel when evidence of Trump’s refusal to cooperate with the investigation—taking classified documents, stonewalling repeated requests to return them, and then trying to mislead federal investigators—was too blatant to ignore. Trump did face one questionable prosecution: Alvin Bragg, the Manhattan prosecutor, charged that his hush money to Stormy Daniels was a campaign-finance violation. But that was not something Biden directed. Besides, Trump’s ambition to imprison his opponents preceded anything Biden did, as anybody who remembers the “Lock her up!” chants should readily concede. Trump was unable to effectively prosecute his enemies during his first term, largely because he was stuck with a Justice Department whose staff was committed to traditional norms of independence, not for lack of trying. To the contrary, Trump spent most of his first term trying to make his attorneys general act like Roy Cohn. He pressured Ukraine’s government to gin up an investigation of Biden, and he eventually appointed a special counsel, John Durham, to investigate various enemies, only for Durham to fall on his face. [ Leo J. Wise: How corruption got this bad ] The most logical way to understand Trump’s motive is that he has always viewed laws as suggestions rather than hard requirements, and tended to assume that people in power will abuse it to protect their friends and punish their enemies. Democratic lawfare did not implant this belief in Trump. He and his allies are going to continue investigating fake crimes and committing real ones, because Trump fundamentally does not believe in the rule of law. What is most peculiar is that the Democrats aren’t the party that has decided to elevate this question in the closing days of the midterm campaign. The Republicans are. Why, you might wonder, did a phalanx of Republicans emerge several days after the fact to start screaming about Slotkin? Anti-anti-Trump Republicans, of which the Journal is a leading voice, often invoke the Mueller investigation and the first Trump impeachment as radicalizing events that reignited their wavering partisan attachment. The misguided Bragg indictment of Trump helped rehabilitate him among Republicans who had been ready to move on after January 6. As Davis wrote on X, “Dear @ElissaSlotkin : You are rallying fractured Republicans right before the midterms.” Trump in his second term has operated with complete impunity. The Republican Congress is not even pretending to conduct oversight over the executive branch, and the Justice Department is not even pretending to care whether the president and his allies follow the law. The president grasps that if he ever has to face accountability, his party will back him up. Trump has two modes: flaunting his impunity and wallowing in victimization. For the moment, he finds the latter more politically useful.

items.title: YEA to deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by November – Basintale
items.description: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) plans to onboard and deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by the end of November 2026 under an agreement with the Ghana Education Service (GES). Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale announced the plan when he addressed the Government Accountability Series at the Jubilee House on Wednesday, October 21. He said the Agency signed a memorandum of understanding with the GES in September to facilitate the recruitment and deployment of the beneficiaries, who are expected to support basic schools, particularly in hard-to-reach communities. The initiative is designed to provide additional teaching support where needed while giving qualified young people practical classroom experience and an opportunity to develop their professional skills. “In this regard, I am happy to report that as recently as September this year, the YEA had signed a successful Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ghana Education Service for the onboarding of some 6000 beneficiaries, who will be deployed by the end of November this year,” Mr Basintale said. The programme is among the Agency’s interventions aimed at combining employment creation with support for essential public services. Mr Basintale said the YEA’s broader mandate was to work with other institutions to provide training, workplace attachment and skills development rather than directly employ beneficiaries into mainstream public and private sector positions.

items.title: Uganda denies Ebola outbreak after Nigeria confirms imported case
items.description: Uganda has denied having an active Ebola outbreak following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), insisting that it has no confirmed active infections as authorities investigate where the patient contracted the virus. In a public statement issued in Kampala on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Uganda’s Ministry of Health said the Nigerian patient had travelled through the country before arriving in Nigeria but stressed that her transit did not establish where she was infected. “We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases,” the ministry said. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: We Call for Calm and Vigilance,” added that preliminary information indicated the woman had travelled through Uganda in early October without symptoms and developed them after arriving in Nigeria. “Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said. It added that Nigeria’s government was expected to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to support further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan authorities also said they were strengthening screening and public health controls at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, announced the confirmed case on Tuesday, saying laboratory tests had established that the woman was infected with Ebola virus disease. According to Pate, the patient had recently travelled to East Africa, including Uganda, before returning to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7. Her condition reportedly worsened four days later, prompting further medical attention and testing. The woman was admitted to a private hospital, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She has since been isolated and is receiving medical care. Pate said health authorities had identified 44 contacts and commenced contact tracing to prevent further transmission. Surveillance has also been strengthened at Nigeria’s points of entry. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare is coordinating the response with the FCT Health Services Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and other public health partners. The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities to remain vigilant and maintain a high index of suspicion for possible Ebola cases, particularly among patients with relevant travel histories and compatible symptoms. He also urged Nigerians to remain calm, practise good hygiene and promptly seek medical attention if they experience symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. Uganda recorded Ebola infections earlier in 2026 but subsequently declared the outbreak over after meeting the required conditions for ending transmission. In its latest statement, the Ugandan Ministry of Health urged the public to remain calm and vigilant, practise regular handwashing and sanitisation, and follow verified updates from official channels. items.title: Un premier cas d’Ebola confirmé à Abuja
items.description: Le Nigeria a annoncé, mardi 20 octobre 2026, la confirmation d’un premier cas d’infection au virus Ebola sur son territoire. La patiente, récemment arrivée d’Ouganda, est prise en charge en isolement dans la capitale, Abuja. Les autorités sanitaires ont lancé le traçage des contacts, tandis que plusieurs pays africains restent confrontés à la circulation du virus. Le Nigeria fait face à son premier cas confirmé d’Ebola. L’information a été annoncée, le mardi 20 octobre 2026 par le ministre de la Santé, Muhammad Ali Pate, après la confirmation de l’infection par des analyses de laboratoire. Selon les informations communiquées par le ministre, la patiente est une femme récemment arrivée d’Ouganda à bord d’un vol international. Elle avait été admise dans un établissement hospitalier privé d’Abuja, où elle a reçu des soins pendant plusieurs jours avant que le diagnostic ne soit établi. Elle est actuellement placée en isolement et bénéficie d’une prise en charge médicale. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement a appelé les structures sanitaires publiques et privées du pays à renforcer leur vigilance et à se mettre en état d’alerte maximale. Cette nouvelle intervient dans un contexte de recrudescence de la maladie sur le continent africain. Depuis mai 2026, la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) est confrontée à la 17ᵉ épidémie d’Ebola de son histoire. D’après les derniers chiffres publiés lundi 19 octobre par les autorités sanitaires congolaises, cette flambée a déjà enregistré 9 455 cas confirmés et 4 561 décès, ce qui en fait la plus meurtrière jamais connue dans le pays. Le Kenya est également concerné par cette dynamique épidémique. Mardi 20 octobre, le pays a signalé un neuvième cas lié à l’épidémie en cours, alors qu’un décès y a déjà été enregistré. La confirmation du cas nigérian vient ainsi renforcer les préoccupations liées à la propagation transfrontalière du virus Ebola en Afrique. Le suivi rigoureux des contacts, le dépistage précoce et l’isolement rapide des personnes infectées demeurent des mesures essentielles pour limiter les risques de transmission et contenir l’épidémie. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un premier cas d’Ebola confirmé à Abuja est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Black Bombers arrive in Kinshasa for 2026 IBA Africa Elite Boxing Championships
items.description: Ghana’s Black Bombers have arrived in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, ahead of the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships. The competition, scheduled to run from October 19 to November 1, will provide the national team with an opportunity to test its readiness against some of the continent’s best boxers. Ghana will be represented by Amadu Mohammed in the bantamweight division (55kg), Ebenezer Ankrah in the lightweight category (60kg) and Joseph “Jaguar” Commey in the light welterweight division (63.5kg). Second lead coach Charles Quartey will head Ghana’s technical team for the championship as the boxers seek to make an impact in Kinshasa. The tournament forms part of Ghana’s preparations for the 2028 Olympic boxing qualifiers, with the Black Bombers targeting strong performances as they build towards the qualifying campaign. Ghana hopes to use the competition to assess its boxers, gain valuable international experience and strengthen its medal prospects ahead of the Olympic qualification process. The team’s participation aligns with its broader ambition to secure multiple medals at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. The championships will bring together elite male and female boxers from across Africa, offering the Ghanaian contingent an important test against continental opposition.

items.title: Élections israéliennes : Netanyahou utilise les violences en France pour renforcer son discours sécuritaire
items.description: Le Premier ministre israelien Benjamin Netanyahou relie directement les recentes violences en France aux consequences du 7-Octobre. Dans un entretien accorde le 20 octobre a i24NEWS, il affirme avoir averti le president francais Emmanuel Macron des 2023 : « Si nous ne les eliminons pas ici, vous les aurez a Paris. » Il ajoute desormais : « Et c'est exactement ce qui se passe. » Netanyahou raconte que Macron l'avait appele apres l'attaque du 7-Octobre pour evoquer une solution diplomatique. Il dit lui avoir repondu que le Hamas devait etre combattu comme l'organisation etat islamique et qu'une strategie d'« apaisement » ne ferait que deplacer la menace vers l'Europe. Interroge sur les troubles en France, il accuse les autorites de ne pas s'etre preparees et d'avoir « cede a l'invasion de l'islam extremiste ». Son conseil a la France est tout aussi direct : : « Battez-vous, ne jouez pas l'apaisement, battez-vous contre les extremistes ». Une comparaison contestee La comparaison est neanmoins tres contestable sur le plan factuel. Les manifestations francaises sont nees de revendications portant notamment sur le coût de la vie et les services publics avant de degenerer, dans plusieurs villes, en pillages et affrontements. Les autorites mettent en cause des groupes d'ultragauche et des casseurs opportunistes. Le rapprochement opere par Netanyahou ne repose sur aucun element tangible. Ces propos surviennent a quelques jours des elections israeliennes du 27 octobre. Netanyahou mene campagne sur la securite, l'Iran et la necessite de maintenir une ligne militaire dure. En invoquant la France, il cherche aussi a presenter le combat mene par Israel depuis le 7 octobre comme une bataille depassant ses propres frontieres et concernant directement l'Europe. La logique israelienne consiste ainsi a montrer que l'etat hebreu est le dernier rempart face a l'islamisme avant qu'il ne deferle sur l'Europe, une ideologie qui s'appuie sur la theorie du « choc des civilisations » du politologue americain Samuel P. Huntington.
